text.p: Falconbridge Ltd said on Friday it increased its nickel output in 1996 by almost 8,000 tonnes.
Nickel output in 1996 totalled 92,000 tonnes, compared with 84,100 tonnes in 1995, Falconbridge said.

Production increased at the Nikkelverk refinery to 61,000 tonnes from 53,200 tonnes in 1995. At Falcondo in Dominican Republic, the company produced 30,400 tonnes of nickel in ferronickel in 1996, compared to 30,900 tonnes in 1995.
Falconbridge also said it signed a memorandum of understanding with the government of Cote d'Ivoire in December for the Touba-Biankouma nickel laterite project.
The memorandum outlined a project schedule and specified the major decision points of the project if it proceeded.
To date, total resources of 195 million tonnes of ore grading 1.55 percent nickel and 0.10 percent cobalt had been identified on the site, Falconbridge said.

The company also expected to sign a memorandum of understanding with the government of Zambia next month to proceed with a feasibility study of the Konkola Deep copper deposit in Zambia. Falconbridge is part of a consortium to develop the deposit, which contains 360 million tonnes of 3.8 percent copper.
Output was expected to reach 180,000 tonnes of finished copper a year.
Meanwhile, Falconbridge blamed its lower fourth-quarter earnings on lower average realized metal prices and higher depreciation and amortization charges due to higher production levels.
The company today reported fourth-quarter earnings of C$27.8 million or C$0.16 a share, down from C$79.8 million or C$0.45 in the year earlier period.
For the year, the nickel company reported profits of C$247.9 million or C$1.40 a share compared to C$333.2 million or C$1.89 a share in 1995.
The company predicted that capital commitments in 1997 would reach C$1 billion, due mainly to construction at the Raglan project in Quebec and the Collahuasi project in Chile.

Falconbridge said it expected to have sufficient funds to finance capital expenditures for the year with current cash levels, funds provided from operations, existing lines of credit and the Collahuasi project financing.
